doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Improvisation as selective composition
summary: Lamb compares improvising to poetry, cites Debussy, Ravel and the Stravinsky quote about composition.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: I’m not sure if there was a specific answer to how it’s done that I’d even want to know because it takes some of the — it’s magic I guess, is what I’m trying to say.

It’s some kind of magic in one sense, and then in another it’s like — I guess it’s like poetry or, you know, having mastered enough of the theoretical knowledge — for me — of you know theory and harmony and playing music, classical music you know, and I’m very influenced by Debussy and Ravel, their beautiful compositions which are very improvised also. You know what’s the Stravinsky quote, that composition is selective improvisation. And that, you know, that’s just the way it is. You sit down, you know as it evolves, but you sit down and you improvise and you go oh my God, I love that theme. And then you start to develop a theme but it’s based off of some sort of improv.
